inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K consolidated cash flow statement, equity-based compensation add-back $31,103k (SFM_10K_FY2025.txt ~line 3120). The 10-K discloses no separate line for taxes paid on net-share settlement, so the add-back is the whole charge; no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure is published.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchase of common stock $471.9m (10-K financing activities, line 3314); H1-2026 $210.0m; Q1-2026 $140.0m. The flat share count is being funded in cash (repurchaser), well in excess of SBC.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 10-Q diluted weighted-average shares 94.41m (quarter ended 2026-06-28); FY2025 diluted 98.704m; dilutive equity awards are ~1.0m of the count. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Continuing buybacks (~1m shares/quarter at ~$70) are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Sunday nearest 31 December (52/53-week year; FY2025 ended 2025-12-28; FY2026 is a 53-week year)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:00Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); Friday close, not after-hours
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 (grocery staples with specialty-retail sensitivity) gives a cost of equity ~9.2%; no funded debt (revolver undrawn since FY2024, only $114m of finance-lease and build-to-suit finance obligations) so WACC ~9.0%. Applied uniformly to all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not through per-scenario discount rates (prior build used 8.5% base / 9.5% bear).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease rent (~$1.86bn of operating lease liabilities at FY2025) is a straight-line SG&A charge, so reported EBITDA and OCF are already post-rent -- leases are in the flows. Only finance-lease liabilities and other finance obligations ($113.8m at Q2-2026) are treated as debt. Not both.
inputs.tax_note: GAAP effective rate 24.0% FY2025 (24.9% FY2024). Cash taxes paid $120.1m FY2025 = 17.5% of EBIT, flattered by stock-based compensation deductions realised at 2025 share prices (~$150) that will not recur at ~$62 and by transferable tax credit discounts. Cash rate ramps 21% -> 24% (21% federal + state) by year 4.
inputs.notes: Fresh Drivers build (the 2026-08-28 DCF was a hand-written 4-year flat-FCF-margin model on a CSV whose FY2020-FY2022 rows were mislabeled/missing and FY2017-18 net income understated; fixed 2026-09-28, commits eafcc11e/3cc5d4d2 -- every driver here is re-judged on the corrected series, not copied). Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row: operating company, consumer). SFM is a US specialty grocer with 500+ company-operated stores, no franchising, no NCI, net cash: the standard operating-company route applies. Interest income not stripped: net interest income was $2.6m in FY2025 and net cash ($110m) is ~0.25x the owner-FCF base, below the 1x materiality rule. FY0 is FY2025 (52 weeks ended 2025-12-28); year 1 is FY2026 (53 weeks), built to management's Q2 guidance: 40+ new stores, comps -0.5%/+0.5%, 53rd week ~+$200m sales/+$28m EBIT, diluted EPS $5.32-5.40 (flat on 52 weeks), net capex $280-310m, buybacks $300m+. Year 2 (FY2027) laps the 53rd week (-2.1% of the base) so its growth rate is below trend; the H1-2026 FCF collapse (-38%) is front-loaded capex (Northern California DC completed in Q2) plus fixed-cost deleverage, not a change in the unit economics. Owner-FCF margin was 5.0% of revenue in FY2025; the component build lands FY2026 at ~4.0% (higher capex, lower margin) and matures at ~4.9%, so the 10-year horizon is used until the margin has settled. Harvest Sherwood's $1bn+ adversary claim (trial 2026-09-21, outcome unknown) is not in the flows or the bridge -- a large adverse judgment would be a bear-scenario event outside this model and is named in key_risks.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025, 6.4%) shaded to 6.0%: unit growth of ~8%/yr on the store base is diluted by new-store productivity and by comps guided to ~0% in FY2026; the equity CAGR (9.7%) is inflated by retained earnings on a buyback-shrunk share count and the 3-year figures start from the FY2022 post-COVID trough.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (30.5%) is nearly 3x revenue 3yr CAGR (11.2%): FY2022-FY2025 EPS growth came from the EBITDA margin expanding from 7.6% to 9.6% and diluted shares falling from 109.1m to 98.7m, not from top-line growth. Equity 5yr CAGR (9.7%) also exceeds revenue 5yr (6.4%) by more than 30%. Both tailwinds are treated as realised: margins are held near the FY2025 level rather than expanded further, and the share count is held flat. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF (SBC-deducted) series: FY2020 owner FCF $357.7m (COVID pantry-loading peak) -> FY2025 $436.6m, FY2022 $230.7m -> FY2025 $436.6m; the owner series grows slightly slower than reported FCF over 5 years (4.1% vs 4.7%) because SBC doubled from $14.3m to $31.1m.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs from the corrected Metrics.csv (2026-09-28 re-export); FY2020 (COVID) is a high starting base for the 5-year figures and FY2022 a low one for the 3-year figures, so neither is a clean trend -- the FY2019-FY2025 six-year revenue CAGR is 7.7%.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +6.7% = ~4.5% from 40+ new stores and flat comps on 52 weeks plus ~2.3% from the 53rd week (FY2026 revenue ~$9.4bn). FY2027 +4.5% laps the 53rd week (-2.1pp) with unit growth ~6% net of new-store ramp and comps +1%. FY2028-30 6.0/5.5/5.0% as ~40 stores/yr shrinks as a share of a 540-620 store base and comps run +1-2%; fades to 3% by year 9 (unit growth ~4%, comps ~inflation).
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA margin here is pre-SBC (FY2025 reported EBITDA $843.9m + SBC $31.1m = 9.94%); FY2026 ~9.45% reflects the guided ~50-75bp fixed-cost deleverage on flat comps (EPS guide $5.32-5.40 on ~95m shares implies EBIT ~$670m on $9.4bn = 7.1% vs 7.8%). Recovers 10bp/yr to 9.8% -- below the FY2025 peak, above the FY2024 8.7% -- as private label (26% of sales) and completed meat/seafood self-distribution offset price investment. D&A 2.0% -> 2.1% (FY2025 1.8%, H1-2026 1.9%, rising with the new-store and DC asset base). Capex gross of landlord reimbursements: FY2026 3.5% ($330m gross vs $280-310m net guidance) easing to 2.8% as openings slow relative to the base; stays above D&A because the store base is still growing. Working capital: grocers run negative working capital, so growth releases a little cash -- 2% of the revenue increase.
base.terminal_rationale: 2.5% terminal growth (mature staples retailer, ~inflation); cap 16x owner FCF. At 9%/2.5% Gordon is 15.8x so Gordon binds.

bull.rationale: Comps turn positive from Q4-2026 (top of the -0.5%/+1.5% Q3 range) and run +3-4% from FY2027 as loyalty personalisation re-engages the budget-sensitive shopper; unit growth steps to 45/yr with the Northeast (New York) format proving out; EBITDA margin rebuilds past the FY2025 peak to 10.8% on private-label mix (26% -> 30%+) and full self-distribution leverage. Capex stays ~3% for the faster opening cadence. Cap 16x binds (Gordon at 9%/3% = 17.2x).

bear.rationale: The negative comps are structural, not a comparison artefact: trade-down to Walmart/Aldi/Costco and conventional grocers' organic aisles keeps comps at -1% to -2% through FY2027 (FY2027 also laps the 53rd week), new-store productivity fades in denser markets, and the new CEO slows openings to ~25/yr. Price investment to answer the affordability problem plus fixed-cost deleverage takes the pre-SBC EBITDA margin back to 8.3% (between FY2023's 7.4% and FY2024's 8.7%). Capex falls with the opening cadence but D&A keeps rising on the built base. Terminal 2.0%, cap 14x for a no-growth grocer.

scenario_narratives.base: Sprouts is a unit-growth story whose comp engine has stalled: after +7.3% comps in FY2025 the company has printed -1.7% and -1.0% and guides flat for the year, so FY2026 revenue growth (~6.7% including a 53rd week) is all new stores. The base case assumes the 2024-25 customer surge finishes unwinding in FY2026, comps settle at +1-2% from FY2027, and 40 stores a year on a 500-store base carries revenue growth of 5-6% through the decade, fading to 3%. Margins do not recover to the FY2025 peak: the pre-SBC EBITDA margin dips to ~9.45% on deleverage and rebuilds to 9.8% as private label and self-distribution offset the price investment management has admitted it needs. Capex stays above D&A for a growing store base, cash taxes normalise to 24% as the 2025 stock-comp deductions fade, and the owner-FCF margin matures at ~4.9%. The axes that matter are (1) whether comps are cyclical or structural, (2) new-store productivity as the format goes east, and (3) how much price Sprouts must give back to keep the less-loyal shopper.
scenario_narratives.bull: Comps re-accelerate to +3-4% once the FY2025 comparison is lapped: Sprouts Rewards (chainwide since Q4-2025) turns customer data into personalised offers that recover basket size, private label climbs past 30% of sales, and completed meat/seafood self-distribution adds gross margin. Unit growth steps up to 45/yr with the Northeast proving out, revenue compounds at 7-8% mid-decade and the EBITDA margin reaches 10.8%, above the FY2025 peak. The stock's 60% fall from the January 2026 high then reverses on both earnings and multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The affordability gap to Walmart, Aldi and Costco is structural for a secondary-destination grocer; comps stay negative through FY2027, the new CEO slows openings, and the margin gives back most of the 2023-25 expansion (pre-SBC EBITDA 8.3%). Revenue growth is 2-3%, the owner-FCF margin settles near 3.5%, and the business is a slow-growth grocer valued at a mid-teens FCF multiple. The Harvest Sherwood $1bn+ claim (trial 2026-09-21, outcome unconfirmed) and the securities class action are tail risks on top of this path, not inside it.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% house default): three consecutive negative-to-flat comp quarters, management's own admission that affordability is a real issue, a CEO transition in January 2027 and an unresolved $1bn+ adversary claim make the structural-slowdown path a live one-in-four outcome, even though the balance sheet (no funded debt, net cash) rules out distress. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs comps to re-accelerate AND margins to exceed the FY2025 peak, two independent things. Base 50%: unit growth is funded and on schedule (500th store opened September 2026) and FY2026 EPS guidance is holding. Same 25/50/25 split as the 2026-08-28 build; the two-sided uncertainty it described has not resolved.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Sprouts as a self-funded store-growth compounder whose comps have gone to zero, not as the +7% comp business of FY2025 and not as a broken retailer. The owner-FCF build charges SBC ($31m, 0.35% of sales) in the flows and holds the share count flat; buybacks ($472m in FY2025, $210m in H1-2026) are how the count stays flat, not a source of value. FY2026 is the guided year (53 weeks, flat comps, EPS ~$5.36, capex up on a completed distribution centre); after that growth is new-store arithmetic on a 500-store base fading from 6% to 3%, margins hold below the FY2025 peak, and a 10-year horizon lets the owner-FCF margin mature (~4.9%) before a Gordon terminal at 2.5% on a 9% USD WACC. Leases are in the flows under ASC 842; only finance obligations are debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: Comps: every 1pp of sustained comp is roughly 1pp of revenue growth AND ~30-40bp of EBITDA margin through fixed-cost leverage; the bear path (comps -1 to -2% through FY2027) is what takes the value to the low $50s.
Harvest Sherwood adversary proceeding ($1bn+ claimed, ~$42m withheld payments; trial 2026-09-21): not modelled. A judgment of even $200-300m would be ~$2-3/share of cash and is not in any scenario.
New-store productivity and cannibalisation as 40+/yr openings move into the Northeast; the base assumes new stores keep earning near-chain-average returns.

Capex: FY2026 gross capex ~$330m is 3.5% of sales vs 2.8% in FY2025; the base assumes it eases to 2.8% -- if openings and remodels keep capex at 3.5% the owner-FCF margin matures ~0.7pp lower (~$10/share).
Cash tax: FY2025's 17.5% cash rate on EBIT depended on stock-comp deductions at ~$150 share prices; the model ramps to 24%, so a return of that benefit is upside, not risk.
CEO succession (Nick Konat, January 2027) during the slowdown; an internal, planned handover but the strategic response to affordability is his to set.

Its JSON also carried a 'weighted_iv_as_published' of 102.64 from an earlier draft; 78.50 is the value the file reported.
